notes.short: Torn-out eyes: they would have given him anything
notes.about: Paul reminds the Galatians how much they once loved him: they would have torn out their eyes for him. The eyes are among the dearest parts of the body, and the saying means they would have given him anything, however dear.

figure.name: Hyperbole
figure.words: torn out your eyes and given them to me
figure.means: the greatest self-sacrifice: they would have given him anything, however dear

notes.evidence: Bullinger lists the verse among examples of Hyperbole. Fausset (Jamieson, Fausset and Brown) calls it a proverbial phrase for the greatest self-sacrifice, the eyes being among the dearest members. Clarke takes it as a proverbial expression for the strongest affection, and Barnes says they would have given him anything, however dear.
notes.limit: Some think the saying was chosen with a weakness in Paul's eyes in mind, as if they would have given him their own in place of his. The verses do not say what his illness was (Galatians 4:13-14).

cites.quote: Other examples of Hyperbole may be seen in 2Sa 17:13. ... Gal 4:15

cites.quote: Dearer than one's eyes, or to profess to give one's eyes for the sake of a person, appears to have been a proverbial expression, intimating the highest tokens of the strongest affection.

cites.quote: No higher proof of attachment could have been given. They loved him so much, that they would have given to him anything, however dear
